title: Smart parking occupancy and gate
intro: A camera and four virtual proximity readings estimate parking-space availability. Only agreement produces a free or occupied decision; disagreement reserves the space. A separate gate state machine requires fresh clear obstruction evidence before closing, including during manual requests. This is a software simulation prototype, not a certified gate controller.
scope: Raspberry Pi targeted, desktop simulation tested. No Pi, real sensor, electrical power, camera timing, motor or physical safety validation was performed. This is an AI-assisted personal engineering project; it does not establish professional seniority or independent authorship.
policies: Space hysteresis uses distance below 70 cm as near and above 90 cm as far; valid distance range is 2 to 400 cm. Camera and sensor agreement produces the decision.
CLOSED transitions to OPENING only when a space is confirmed free; the virtual opening takes two seconds.
OPEN or HOLD requires two seconds of fresh clear evidence to enter CLOSING. Any obstruction or invalid evidence during closure moves to HOLD.
Actuator failure enters FAULT. Reset requires stable clear evidence and returns to OPEN for inspection. Restart during a gate cycle enters FAULT.
model: YOLO11n detects car, motorcycle, bus and truck; person detections feed the obstruction flag. The weights remain pretrained. Float32 ONNX at 640 replaces a 320-pixel baseline, with threshold 0.25 selected on 42 validation images. Detection matches use class-aware greedy IoU >= 0.5 on 78 test images. This is not official COCO AP; ignored crowd regions can still generate false positives.
tradeoff: Higher resolution increased vehicle F1 from 0.386 to 0.581 at roughly 3.6 times detector latency. Conservative fusion eliminated 15 false-free slot-seconds on the scripted trace, but only 83.33% of slot-seconds received a definite decision. Accuracy on decided slots was 100%; counting unknowns as errors gives 83.33%, below the baseline 93.75%. Reserving uncertainty costs availability.
limitations: The four image regions are example vertical lanes, not calibrated real parking spaces. COCO object F1 is not parking occupancy accuracy. Only one motorcycle ground-truth instance occurs in the held-out test. Reflections, occlusion and shadows were explored with transformations, not a labeled parking deployment dataset. A stop/HOLD software state does not physically reopen a gate. Independent obstruction hardware, limit switches and electrical interlocks remain required.

Restore devices, request close and advance time to demonstrate the clear-evidence delay. Select a real COCO sample and run inference; its regions are examples, not calibrated spaces.
bom: Raspberry Pi 4 or 5, USB camera, four HC-SR04 distance sensors or verified 3.3 V proximity modules, independent break-beam obstruction sensor, small bench servo, two limit switches, separate regulated servo supply and common signal ground.
wiring: Example BCM allocation: trigger/echo pairs (5,6), (13,19), (20,21), (23,24); obstruction input GPIO17; servo signal GPIO18; open/closed limit inputs GPIO22/27. Use an appropriate divider or level shifter on every 5 V echo line. GPIO numbering is BCM, not physical header numbering.
resume: Implemented a Raspberry Pi–targeted parking simulator with camera/proximity fusion, explicit gate states and an obstruction interlock that also applies to manual requests.
Improved vehicle F1 from 0.386 to 0.581 on 78 held-out COCO images by increasing inference resolution, with class-level results and host timing evidence.
Eliminated 15 false-free slot-seconds and 14 unsafe closure requests in separate synthetic comparisons, reporting 83.33% availability-decision coverage.
